subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference costs and unit economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@finbot.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finbot.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — inference costs and unit economics

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned. Let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points
- Inference unit economics: 5-6x higher than target for your core prediction pipeline when running on current GCP instances (we discussed 3-4M predictions/day as baseline).
- Latency SLO pressure: need ~200 ms p95 for the API powering the product experience.
- Workload shape: many short requests (avg tokens ~60), a few long-context flows for analytics.
- No consistent batching or KV cache layer today; most requests are single-shot to a replicated pod fleet.
- Willingness to explore quantization but concerned about subtle quality regressions for your fraud detection prompts.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Self-hosted Llama 2 variants on GCP A2-like VMs, custom orchestration, Triton in front for model serving.
- In-house autoscaling but limited batching due to how requests flow through the product.
- Logs and evals are in S3; you have a small labeled set (~2k examples) for regression testing.

Success criteria (how you said you will evaluate a vendor)
- Reduce per-prediction unit cost by ~2.5-3x without exceeding 200 ms p95.
- Maintain classification/regression quality: fewer than 2% drop vs current baseline on your eval set.
- POC completed in ~3-4 weeks with runbook for production roll-forward.

Redwood proposed approach
- Quick cost model and POC using a dedicated pool (we can show expected unit economics with batching and KV caching).
- Validate INT8/INT4 quantization on your eval set to measure quality delta.
- Technical deep-dive next week to collect workload traces / sample payloads (so we can size batching and cache policy).

Next steps (agreed)
1) I will share a scoped POC doc and a rough pricing estimate (attached). [Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx]
2) Please share a few representative request traces and a small eval sample (anonymized) — upload to the Drive link we agreed on.
3) Tech deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer (Rishi) — Rishi suggested Wed or Thu next week.
4) Procurement: you said FinBot would aim to decide by end of Q2; we will align POC timing to that window.

Attachments
- redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, ~42KB)
- poc-scope.md (POC scope doc, ~3KB)

Thanks — I'll follow up with calendar invites and the Drive upload link.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)]

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications:
- The 5-6x cost number is what our finance model reports today vs what we think would be acceptable; we are targeting ~50% reduction to start (stretch 3x by end of year).
- We can surface 1 week of request traces and a 2k-label eval set; I'll anonymize PII.
- Procurement timeline: we have a budget review the week of Apr 20 and would like a POC completed before that review if possible.

We're generally open to quantization experiments as long as there's a solid regression testing plan.

I'm available next Wed (Mar 11) 10-12 PT or Thu (Mar 12) 14-16 PT for the tech deep-dive.

Alex

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@finbot.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — inference costs and unit economics

Alex / Marissa,

Quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive. Thanks for sharing the traces — those will be the most useful artifact. A few asks to make the POC high-signal:
- Please include raw request payloads (no PII) and the sequence length distribution; we use that to size batching windows and kernel selection.
- Tell us which model variants you currently run (e.g., Llama2-13B, custom finetune tags) and whether you can run a quantized build for experiments (we can also run the quantized variant on our side if you prefer).
- KV cache behavior: do you have many multi-turn sessions where prefix caching will help? If so, provide an example flow.

What we plan to validate in the POC:
1) Unit-cost model with enabling batching + prefix/KV caching. We'll show a per-100k request cost delta and sensitivity to batch size.
2) Quantization test (INT8 and INT4 where feasible) with your eval set to measure quality delta.
3) Latency regressions: ensure p95 stays within your 200 ms target under a realistic arrival pattern.

For the deep-dive I can run through an execution plan and what artifacts we need. Either Mar 11 10am PT or Mar 12 2pm PT works on my side — Marissa, can you confirm what you prefer and I'll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
[Attachment: poc-scope.md (text, 3KB)]
